opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Running the warehouses, paying staff and the back office.

follow100Note: Membership fees are only $1.95 of every $100 — but they arrive with almost no cost attached, which is why they cover nearly two-thirds of the profit Costco keeps. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Costco's merchandise costs include buying, freight and shrink (lost or damaged goods) — the direct cost of what's on the shelves.
otherDetail: Interest income and other of $155M, less $32M of interest expense.

segments.name: Net sales
segments.note: Everything sold in the warehouses and online. Comparable sales rose 9.8% (6.6% adjusted for gasoline prices and currency).

segments.name: Membership fees
segments.note: Annual membership fees — almost pure profit, and the engine that lets Costco keep merchandise prices low.

takeaways.text: Comparable sales rose 9.8% (6.6% after adjusting for gasoline prices and currency), and digitally-enabled sales jumped 21.5% — more members spending more per trip.
takeaways.title: Shoppers kept coming

takeaways.text: Membership fees rose 10.7% to $1.37B. Merchandise itself earns a thin 12.8% gross margin by design — the fees are where the money is.
takeaways.title: Fees quietly fund the profit

takeaways.text: Net income rose 15% to $2.19B, faster than the 11.6% sales growth, as warehouse operating costs (SG&A) grew more slowly than revenue.
takeaways.title: Profit outgrew sales

verdict: Costco's net sales rose 11.6% to $69.2B as comparable sales jumped 9.8% — and with $1.37B of nearly cost-free membership fees on top, profit rose 15% to $2.19B.
